doc: Rules for the root-cause evidence graph (brief PHASE 3C). An engineer can read and edit this file; the graph builder reads it at runtime and never hardcodes these links in Python.
justification_source: backend/app/simulator/mechanisms.py — the generator's mechanism table. Every entry there names the sensor channel a fault pushes (process_physics.FAULT_SEVERITY), the spatial signature it paints on the wafer (Mechanism.spatial_signature) and the yield loss it causes (Mechanism.yield_loss_pp). These rules restate those physics links for the ENGINE's candidate set; they do not read ground truth.

edge_semantics.kind_measured: strength comes from this lot's own data (feature snapshot, wafer pattern, yield/defect density)
edge_semantics.kind_rule: strength comes from this file; the evidence link is the rule_id, which is auditable text, not a hidden constant

candidate_rules.justification: mechanisms.MECHANISMS['rf_power_drift'] pushes the rf_power channel and paints Edge-Ring (edge_bias 0.55) with a 0.05 scratch bias; yield_loss_pp 8.5.

candidate_rules.mechanism: Chamber pressure instability driving particle generation
candidate_rules.justification: mechanisms.MECHANISMS['chamber_pressure_instability'] pushes pressure, paints Edge-Ring (edge_bias 0.65), particle_multiplier 7.0; yield_loss_pp 10.0 — the strongest edge-biased mechanism in the table.

candidate_rules.mechanism: Recipe-transition stress with a gas-flow offset
candidate_rules.justification: FAULT_SEVERITY offsets gas_flow first (and pressure second) for recipe_transition_problem, which paints Loc (edge_bias 0.20, scratch_bias 0.10); yield_loss_pp 6.5.

candidate_rules.mechanism: Thermal excursion with in-chamber particle condensation
candidate_rules.justification: No dedicated temperature fault exists; the table's Donut-painting mechanisms (sensor_drift yield_loss_pp 7.0 and contamination_event yield_loss_pp 13.0) are the thermal/condensation family, so a temperature excursion is mapped to them with a lower edge strength than the direct channels.

candidate_rules.mechanism: Over-etch / etch-time deviation with edge-biased removal
candidate_rules.justification: etch_time is an etch-process parameter; the table reaches edge-biased removal only through the edge_bias of the pressure/RF mechanisms (0.65/0.55), so this is mapped at a deliberately weaker strength than the sensor channels.

candidate_rules.mechanism: Tool degradation (worsens with days since maintenance)
candidate_rules.justification: mechanisms.MECHANISMS['equipment_degradation'] paints Scratch (scratch_bias 0.55, particle_multiplier 6.0) and is reset by maintenance; yield_loss_pp 5.5.

candidate_rules.mechanism: Tool degradation (worsens with days since maintenance)
candidate_rules.justification: Same mechanism as Equipment Yield History — failure history is the other observable surface of the same degradation process (yield_loss_pp 5.5).

candidate_rules.mechanism: Tool degradation (worsens with days since maintenance)
candidate_rules.justification: The degradation mechanism is defined by days-since-maintenance, so an overdue tool maps to it at the highest strength of the three condition candidates.

unmapped_candidates.Voltage: No entry in the generator's mechanism table pushes voltage; an electrical excursion has no authored physical mechanism, so the graph shows the sensor-issue node with no mechanism edge rather than inventing one.
unmapped_candidates.Current: Same as Voltage — no authored mechanism.

defect_to_yield_loss.note: The defect-pattern -> yield-loss edge strength is MEASURED from this lot's defect density (0-1) and its distance below the low-yield threshold; nothing here is a constant.
